continuity_scope: Supergiant Games Hades v1.0 launch on 17 September 2020 for Nintendo Switch, Steam, and Epic Games Store. This pass uses the release announcement/FAQ as the fixed witness, not Early Access builds, later PC patches, 2021 PlayStation/Xbox versions, 2024 iOS/Netflix version, Hades II, or other adaptations. The launch itself added a true ending, new events, a weapon variant, a final-boss variant, and late-game unlocks; none of their outcomes are generalized here.
work_or_witnesses: Supergiant Games, Hades: Now Out of Early Access!
Supergiant Games, Pre-Order: PUP Zagreus & Nendoroid Megaera
coverage_rule: Only individual game characters directly given an unambiguous role/designation by the selected Supergiant launch or product text: Zagreus ('immortal Prince of the Underworld'), Hades ('god of the dead' whom the game asks the player to defy), and Megaera ('First of the Furies'). This is intentionally not a full cast. The selected official launch notice says there are thirty voiced characters but does not supply a complete profile index; all other names in patch/event lists are omitted rather than rebuilt from fan databases. Olympians, underworld groups, boons, weapons, places, runs, and systems are terms/dimensions.
omissions: Nyx, Achilles, Thanatos, Dusa, Charon, Persephone, Olympian deities, Furies, shades, bosses, and all other named or unnamed game figures not role-profiled under this deliberately narrow witness rule.

All player-selected boons, weapons, aspects, keepsakes, difficulty settings, dialogue/affinity progression, repeated run outcomes, story order, boss variants, endings, and every mutable build or relationship state.

Early Access versions and early-ending variants, post-launch patches, PlayStation/Xbox/iOS versions, merchandise depictions, Hades II early-access/full-release content, crossovers, classical/modern Greek textual traditions as independent sources, fan wikis, Wikipedia, guides, and community databases.
uncertainties: Supergiant's retained official pages are launch/FAQ/product materials rather than an exhaustive Hades character codex. The three-card scope is complete against the stated role-identification rule only.

The game explicitly reimagines a Greek-myth Underworld. These are Supergiant's game-character interpretations; no claim is made that their parentage, powers, temperament, relationships, or chronology match any ancient or living tradition.
Hades is a single-player rogue-like, whose narrative and character events unfold across repeated escape attempts. Dialogue, affinity, and ending progression are therefore not fixed record attributes.
evidence_basis: Supergiant Games first-party launch, FAQ, and official product-post evidence only. No fan or secondary source is used as canonical evidence.

supports: v1.0 date/platforms, 30 voiced characters, launch-content boundary, Zagreus, god-of-the-dead opposition, Olympian powers, mythic weapons, Underworld, and repeat-attempt structure
